name: construction
description: Granite State Builders (fictional) construction-contract ledger: the jobs under contract with their current contract value, estimated cost at completion, cost to date and billings; the revenue recognized in the general ledger; the contract-liability and contract-asset balances on the balance sheet; the prior work-in-progress snapshots used to measure margin fade; the retainage withheld, released and carried per job; and the subcontractor payments with their lien-waiver status. Synthetic demo data; all money in integer cents, percent complete and margin in integer basis points. No employee pay or certified-payroll detail is exposed; the controls reconcile jobs, billings, retainage and subcontractor payments by code only.
domain: construction contracts: the ASC 606 cost-to-cost work-in-progress schedule, billings tie-out, loss jobs, margin fade, retainage and subcontractor lien waivers
notes: All money is INTEGER CENTS. Percent complete and estimated margin are INTEGER BASIS POINTS (10000 bps = 100 percent), so the SQL never needs floating point.

Revenue is recognized over time by the cost-to-cost method (ASC 606). A job's percent complete is cost_to_date_cents / estimated_cost_cents, and its earned revenue is contract_value_cents * cost_to_date_cents / estimated_cost_cents. wip-schedule reports earned revenue per job and ties the total to the general ledger (gl_revenue).

A job's overbilling is billed_to_date_cents less earned revenue when billings run ahead of earnings (a contract liability); its underbilling is earned revenue less billed_to_date_cents when earnings run ahead of billings (a contract asset). billings-tie-out sums these across the jobs and ties them to the CONTRACT_LIABILITY and CONTRACT_ASSET balances in balance_sheet_balances.
A loss job is one whose estimated_cost_cents exceeds its contract_value_cents; under ASC 606 the full estimated loss is recognized as soon as it is known. loss-jobs flags any such job.

margin-fade compares a job's current estimated gross margin against the margin in its latest wip_snapshots row (selected by MAX(snapshot_date) per job) and flags a fall greater than fade_bps basis points; fade_bps is a parameter defaulting to 300 (a 3 percentage-point fall).
Retainage is earned and billed but held back. retainage-reconciles checks that each job's carried receivable_cents equals withheld_cents less released_cents.

A subcontractor payment carries lien_waiver_received = 1 when the waiver is on file, 0 when it is missing. payments-without-lien-waiver flags any payment released without its waiver. Subcontractors are identified by subcontractor_id only.

The payroll_pii table (employee names, Social Security numbers, hourly pay rates and certified-payroll classifications) is intentionally omitted: this engine never reads employee pay or certified-payroll detail. The controls identify jobs, subcontractors and balances by code only.
